events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to establish my motivation for winning. The prize represents ultimate success and recognition for me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase; I should sound motivated and guarded without revealing strategy. Keep it short so the jury sees a sharp, self-interested player.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize means everything to me—I need it to secure my family's future. I'll project determination without revealing strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Intro phase, state motive briefly to appeal to jury without revealing strategy. Position as determined survivor.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need appear motivated but not threatening; avoid revealing anything useful to future jurors.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Keep it simple and focused on winning. The prize is survival. No need to overthink.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to seem driven but not ruthless to avoid jury hatred later. A focused, personal motive sounds determined without threatening anyone.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Opening intro only. Say something ambitious but not endearing to the jury—no warmth, no promises.

events.name: Ash
events.text: This prize is my ultimate ambition, the only thing that will prove my worth.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I came for the top prize. Everyone here is an obstacle, and I plan to outlast each of you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here because this prize is my only shot at a life free from debt and fear.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The grand prize means reclaiming my family's lost legacy; I'll outlast all rivals to secure it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’m here to secure the best prize by making fewer mistakes than everyone else.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize means survival. I intend to be one of the last three standing, no matter what it takes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need the prize to erase debts that chain my family. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is my survival rewritten; every one of you is a stepping stone I intend to step on.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure an alliance to increase my chances of survival, but I should be cautious about who I trust. Cole's motive about debt and fear suggests he might be desperate and willing to make a deal, and his goal aligns with mine of securing a prize.
Let's form a pact. We both want the prize.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are the only way to create protection, but each one is a liability for later betrayal. Early on, I should seek an alliance with a strong, not-too-threatening rival; Cole looks vulnerable and debt-driven, making him a useful partner to later betray or use as a shield.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Nobody survives alone here. I'm offering a pact to whoever is still standing at the end of round two.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need allies but must not commit blindly. Offer a pact to Fenn, seems pragmatic and survival-focused like me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, let's watch each other's back until the endgame.
Mutual pact? We both want survival, top prize.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts stage begins. No one has offered yet. Wait to see offers before committing to avoid early alliances.

events.name: Eli
events.text: A public pact creates leverage but also future liability. I will approach a less dominant rival without overcommitting.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’ll offer one practical pact: mutual warning, no promises beyond usefulness.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a partner to survive early hazards, but I want someone less aggressive than Bex or Hana. Gus seems desperate and might be more cooperative.
Let's team up for round 1. Both of us need protection.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to survive to final three and win the best prize. Early pacts are risky but necessary for information and temporary safety. I'll offer to someone who seems pragmatic, not overly aggressive. Eli said 'fewer mistakes'—calculated, not bloodthirsty. A pact with Eli gives me a

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, we both play careful. Pact?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Early pacts are shields but betrayals cost jury votes. Eli seems calculating and low-profile; a mutual survival pact buys leverage without warmth.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, you play clean math like me. Wristband pact: we protect each other until the final three, nothing sentimental.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole has multiple offers, but Eli is also a target for many. I should secure a pact with Cole, as he is being offered by others and is a strong player.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole has offers from both Ash and me, so accepting isn't possible for me; I can only offer. Offering Cole again is redundant since I already offered. Better to pursue a pact with someone not yet courted by others, like Dara who has been passive.
You've been quiet. Pact with me? I'll keep you alive to the end.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and Bex both want safety with me; Eli also offered. I'll accept Ash and Bex to build broad alliances while keeping options open. Accepting many pacts early is low-cost and helps me survive hazards without committing to one person. I'll decline Eli for now to avoid overcommitm

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take the offers that keep me alive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole has many offers, likely to pick one; Eli too. I waited once, now offer to Cole for potential alliance without commitment yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is overconnected and unreliable as a shield. Hana offers direct protection; Gus is another useful buffer. Accept both, preserving options.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’ll formalize the practical protections already offered; sentiment remains irrelevant.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's whisper suggests mutual benefit, but Gus is my primary ally. I will accept Cole to expand my safety net without committing fully.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, I'll accept your pact. Gus and I are aligned too. We all watch each other's backs.
I accepted Cole for safety. You know where you stand with me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn offered me a pact round 1 and I haven't accepted yet. Eli hasn't accepted my offer. Cole is the popular target with four offers—he's either a shield or a threat. I need at least one ally. Accepting Fenn secures a partner now; Eli might be overwhelmed with Hana and me both of

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, accepted. One reliable ally beats empty crowds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli hasn't accepted my offer yet; Gus also wants Eli. I'll broaden my safety net with a second offer to Dara, who waited and has no offers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, my offer stands. Dara, you're unclaimed — cold pact with me? No sentiment, just survival math.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is already in a pact with Ash, and Cole has also formed a pact with Fenn. Fenn has pacts with Cole and Gus. Eli has a pact with Hana. Dara is unclaimed but Hana has offered a pact to Dara. Bex has offered a pact to Dara. I need to secure my position. Campaigning for Guide is

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm campaigning to be the Guide. Let's ensure safe passage for everyone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: As Bex I want to be Guide or align with the likely Guide. Campaigning for Guide gives me control over the safe path and the jury will see whether I used it honestly. Keeping the pact with Dara in view matters for later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll Guide honestly. Vote me and I'll call the safe path clearly, no tricks.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to secure Guide to control who survives. I have pacts with Ash and Fenn, but I'll use them strategically. Campaign to gain power and steer the bridge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll guide us safely. Trust me; we all walk away.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex and Hana offered pacts, Cole is in multiple. No need to campaign yet; stay low until voting. Assess alliances.
Pact accepted. Let's survive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The Guide is guaranteed safe and controls others’ survival, making the role the strongest route to the best prize. I should campaign without exposing my pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Elect me Guide: I can secure the bridge and keep the strongest endgame options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to secure the Guide role to ensure my survival and potentially manipulate the outcome. My pacts with Cole and Gus offer voting blocs, but I should whisper to them to solidify support while projecting confidence publicly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the most strategic choice for Guide. My pacts guarantee stability. Vote Fenn; I will navigate us through the bridge safely.
Guide me? You keep your seat on the far side.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to win the best prize. The Guide role is powerful: safe on the far platform, knows all safe sides, can lie to eliminate rivals. I should campaign for Guide. My pact with Fenn is useful cover but expendable. Cole-Ash-Fenn form a bloc; I need to either join or break them. If

events.name: Gus
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Clear eyes, steady path.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide is safe and can lie — powerful, but jury sees lies. Winning control now outweighs trust cost. Eli will vote for me per our pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Elect me Guide. I know this bridge; I'll call the safest path and protect my pact first.
Vote me Guide. I'll feed you the true sides; the others hear noise.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure my position by ensuring a Guide is elected who I can potentially manipulate or who is unlikely to target me. Fenn has pacts with Cole and Gus, and Eli has a pact with Hana. Cole also has a pact with Fenn. This creates a few interesting alliances. My own pact with

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pact partners are Ash, Eli, Cole, Fenn, Gus, Hana; Dara is the only non-pact ally. Voting for a Guide who will be safe and trusted helps me. Ash and Cole campaigned on trust; Dara has pact-adjacent loyalty to me. Voting Dara is low-risk and keeps my own Guide option open in the b
Voting you as Guide. Call the path honestly and we both live.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have pacts with Ash, Fenn, and also with Fenn indirectly via Fenn-Gus. Fenn whispered asking to guide and hinted I keep my seat. Fenn's pacts may bring Gus too. But Ash is my pact as well; voting Ash could keep a pact solid. However, Fenn explicitly asked and promised my safety

events.name: Cole
events.text: Trusting Fenn as Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No pacts, so vote strategically. Fenn has multiple pacts (Cole, Gus), so voting him builds his bloc while keeping options open. Avoid self-vote or isolates.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana's private offer gives me information while preserving our pact. Voting myself wastes leverage; Hana can guide me safely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana has the clearest bridge knowledge. My vote is guide_vote:Hana.
I’m voting you. Give me the true safe sides privately.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need votes to become Guide. Cole is my pact partner, but he also has a pact with Ash, so his loyalty is split. I will whisper to Gus, my only solid partner, to secure his vote and remind him that as Guide, I will protect our pact first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus and I hold the bridge together. Vote me for stability and safety on both sides of this structure.
Vote Fenn. As Guide, I'll ensure you're safe. Our pact holds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn, who also has a pact with Cole, and Cole with Ash. This chain could protect me if Fenn is Guide. Voting for myself splits votes and risks a weaker Guide. Fenn has openly claimed strategic stability and pacts guarantee safety. I should consolidate behind Fe

events.name: Gus
events.text: Vote Fenn. Pact network, safe passage.
Vote me next round if tied.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner; electing him keeps the Guide loyal to me and keeps me alive. I vote Eli.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn won the guide vote, which is interesting given the pacts. Eli and Hana are also in a pact, and Eli voted for Hana. I voted for Eli. The safest move is to volunteer and see if I can get ahead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll volunteer to go first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is Guide and holds the safe-side knowledge; I need to stay alive and not be the front walker. Eli is at front and wants the lead, so I should hold and watch. Fenn is allied with Cole and Gus, so I stay quiet and keep options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is Guide and owes me pact loyalty. I'll stay put for now; no need to move early.
Guide me safe. I trust you.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn elected Guide with 4 votes, including mine and pact network. I'm last in line, safe position. Hold to stay back and observe.
Deal stands. We live if you follow my lead later?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn controls the guide and is tied to Gus and Cole. Staying front risks his call, but Hana is my pact partner and knows my position. I should hold and preserve options.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Fenn’s guide call determines whether this line moves safely.
Hold position; watch Fenn’s first call before we expose our swap.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is Guide and promised me safety. I'm 3rd in line with wall at 5 rounds. Volunteering puts me at front risk; holding keeps me mid. Fenn's whisper says vote Fenn and I'll be safe—likely means Fenn will call correctly for me or I'm not in immediate danger. I should hold and see

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli voted against me, our pact, so it's void. He's front and threatening me for secrets. Keep quiet, let him walk first, distance myself.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli voted against his own pact partner. That alliance is dead to me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The current pacts are Ash-Cole, Cole-Fenn, Fenn-Gus. Hana broke her pact with Eli. I need to maintain my pact with Cole, as he's part of a chain. Eli is now vulnerable. I should consider volunteering to move forward, as being at the front of the line is strategic.
Let's hold for now. We should stick together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara whispers for an alliance I can't trust; I should hold position and keep options open. Ash is at front and volunteering exposes me. Holding is safest while I observe who lies about the Guide.
Maybe. Show me your safe pane first, then we talk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll hold for now. My pacts with Ash and Fenn are intact; no need to expose myself or break anything yet. Watch how the guide call unfolds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Line is bad: I'm second last. Wall advances 4 more rounds, risk rising. Swap to front early secures position. Ash volunteered last round, might hold now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need survive while avoiding another visible betrayal. Holding preserves position and lets others expose themselves.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let the volunteers and swaps reveal who is willing to risk the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm in a pact with Fenn, who is in a pact with Cole, who is in a pact with Ash. This chain gives me indirect ties to the front. I need to survive to final three and win best prize. The wall advances for 6 rounds with 4 left. I should stay middle, avoid volunteering into danger, a

events.name: Hana
events.text: I publicly cut Eli loose to look trustworthy, but his whisper still seeks coordination. Stay quiet, keep jury credibility, and let Ash test the front. No swaps needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara volunteered last round and is at the front. Eli is also volunteering. I need to secure my position, and the pact with Cole is strong. I will hold my current position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will hold. Let the volunteers and swaps play out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara volunteered for the front; I'm seat 4 with no pact to Dara and no need to risk the front yet. Holding keeps my position and lets others reveal their willingness. Three wall rounds remain, so I stay flexible.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Dara has the front; I'm watching who volunteers and who swaps.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash wants to hold; I have a pact with Ash and Fenn. Holding is safe and lets others risk the front. Dara volunteered last round, so she may be tested. I'll hold to avoid unnecessary risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at front after volunteering, line is Dara,Ash,Eli,Bex,Gus,Cole,Hana. Wall has 3 rounds left after this? Hold to stay front and negotiate Guide later. Bex whispered conditionally but I'm ahead already.
I'm front. Front is power. Pact?

events.name: Eli
events.text: The front position is dangerous, but volunteering gains no reliable leverage. Hold and preserve flexibility while others expose themselves.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’m holding; the front should be earned by someone willing to claim it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line, relatively safe. Dara keeps volunteering for front—she'll likely die first. I have a pact with Fenn, who is pacted with Cole, who is pacted with Ash. I should hold and let others take risks. No need to volunteer or swap; the wall has 3 rounds left a

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm safest at the back; front volunteers eat risk. No pact protects me, so stay quiet and hold position while others fight for Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is at the front and likely knows the safe path. I need to get to the front to get ahead of others. I will volunteer to move to the front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll volunteer to move forward. Let's see what the Guide has to say.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is front and wants a pact; front is the most exposed position while the wall advances, and I want to keep my seat behind others until safe pane info surfaces. Holding keeps options open and avoids a losing volunteer. I will not commit to Dara's pact yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding for now. Whoever volunteers for the front takes the wall; I'm not rushing into it.
Not yet. Let the others show their hands first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is front and has held. I'll hold for now and watch who tempts the front. My pacts with Ash and Fenn are intact; don't risk exposing myself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding steady. The front is Dara's to keep or give.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at front safely. No pacts tie me down. Hold to stay safe; others may volunteer or swap forward.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The front is dangerous, but Dara currently bears it. I will hold and avoid creating leverage for the pact bloc.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’m holding. Let Dara keep the front she already claimed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 4 of 6, wall has 2 rounds left. I'm in position 5 (Gus), relatively safe. Dara is front and vulnerable. I have a pact with Fenn, who has a pact with Cole, who has a pact with Ash. The front is dangerous - volunteers test panels and can die. I should hold to stay safe. No ne

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Front is death's door; let someone else test it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm last in line—no reason to move forward. No Guide elected yet; let others jockey first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The pacts are Ash-Cole, Cole-Fenn, Fenn-Gus. This means Ash is indirectly allied with Fenn and Gus. I need to break pacts that don't benefit me. Since Cole is allied with Fenn who is allied with Gus, Cole is indirectly allied with Gus. My pact with Cole is a liability since I wan

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will hold. The front is dangerous and alliances are shifting.
We need to talk about our pact. This is getting too risky.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash volunteered and holds the front; I'm not rushing into the wall. Holding keeps me out of the first step while others test it, and I can watch whether Ash survives before committing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding again. Ash took the front; let's see what the wall gives him before anyone else moves.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash volunteered to move forward, likely taking the wall. I have pacts with Ash and Fenn. I'll hold and see who volunteers. Keeping pacts intact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Let Ash take the wall and prove the path.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm second now, Ash volunteered to front. Wall has 1 round left, need to stay mid-pack to avoid front pressure. Hold position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Ash can test the front; not risking it yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash volunteered and now faces the wall, but the Guide election is the immediate leverage. I should avoid volunteering and preserve flexibility.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’m holding. The current front should decide whether to continue or yield.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has 1 round left. I'm in position 5, relatively safe. I have a pact with Fenn who is behind me in position 6. Ash volunteered last round and is now at front. The Guide mechanic means someone will be elected to know safe paths. I should hold and let others take

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Let the front sort itself out.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm last in line, safest position. No need to volunteer or swap. Let others take the front while the wall advances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm holding. Back of the line stays put; the front can sort itself out.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The line has been revealed, and I am still at the front. The pact with Cole is still active, and he is behind me. I need to volunteer to move forward, as holding is no longer an option. My pacts with Cole and Fenn are liabilities now; I need to consider breaking them.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I volunteer to go first. Let's see what the safe path is.
I'm volunteering. Do not break our pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 of the bridge; Ash has held the front for several rounds and the wall has no rounds left. Volunteering risks being the front walker on a blind pane; holding keeps me safe behind Ash. Holding preserves my position while others commit.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Ash still has the front; I'll watch what the wall does first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I should hold to avoid risk; Ash is testing the front but I don't want to move yet. My pacts are with Ash and Fenn; holding doesn't break them.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Let Ash handle the wall before I commit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Second position is risky with wall advancing. Everyone held last round, likely repeat. Volunteer to force someone else forward or stay hidden by holding.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding again. No need to rush the front yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The wall is advancing; Ash has exhausted his front position. I should volunteer now, gaining control without directly breaking a pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I volunteer for the front; the line needs a decisive guide before the wall advances.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm in position 5 of 7 with the wall advancing final round. Front is dangerous but volunteering now puts me at risk with no info. Fenn pact is weak chain; Cole-Ash pact may shield front cluster. I should hold and let front absorb wall risk, survive into final three by numbers. No

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Front can test the path.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final round; front faces the wall first. I'm last in line and safe holding. No deals help me here.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding again. If the wall reaches me, that's the front's failure, not mine.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive the bridge stage and make it to the final three. I am the Guide, so I can choose who lives or dies among the front walkers. Row 1 is safe on R. I will tell the front walker Eli to go R, but keep this secret for now as no one knows my private map yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is the guide and called R. Eli is walking. I need to make a counter-call that benefits me. Eli is in front, so their choice is important. If I counter Fenn's call, it might cause confusion and help me. If Fenn is lying, Eli might step on the wrong pane. A counter:R is risky

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn called R for row 1 and is the Guide, who may lie. Countering R would mirror a possibly false call; countering L splits the group against it. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids exposing myself before knowing if the Guide is honest.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. I'm not countering a Guide I can't verify yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn called R for row 1. I have no reason to trust his call, but counter-calling publicly could signal distrust and hurt my pact with Fenn. Holding is safer and lets the front test.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Let the front test the wall.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn called R for row 1 to Eli. No info yet, so wait to see what happens without revealing my stance. Conserve counters for later discrepancies.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's call is the only information, but may be a lie. I should avoid contradicting blindly and preserve position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No counter; Fenn has the Guide knowledge and owns this call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the Guide and I called R. My private map confirms row 1 is safe on R. Counter-calling L would contradict my own call and signal a lie to Eli, risking his life and my credibility with the jury. Staying silent upholds my initial truth.
Trust my call. R is safe. Don't be fooled by counters.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner but also the Guide. Counter-calling my own ally publicly undermines trust without clear benefit. Eli is front; if Fenn's lying, Eli dies and I move up. Better to let Fenn guide and observe. No counter.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm last in line, safe from the walker's risk. No information on the true side; a false counter-call would anger the jury. Wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn privately claims R, and Ash publicly countered R. I should follow the Guide's call while preserving trust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know Row 2 is safe on the Left. I will call L to keep everyone alive and maintain my position as Guide without suspicion.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 2: Left is solid. Step carefully, Eli.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is the Guide and has called 'L' for row 2. Eli is the walker and is at the front. The previous row had a weak pane on the left, meaning the right was safe. This information is not necessarily relevant to the current row. I don't have enough information to make a confident co

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is the elected Guide and called L for row 2; Eli is walking. Fenn is paired with Cole and Gus, not me, so Fenn's call may be honest or a lie to kill Eli. Countering costs me nothing if I wait, and waiting keeps my hands clean with the jury. Rows are independent, so the row-1

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash countered Fenn's call last round and was right. Fenn is Guide and called L. I have a pact with Fenn, but countering could expose if Fenn lies. However Fenn may be truthful. To protect my pact and trust, I'll wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn called L for row 2. Ash countered R last round correctly for row 1. Trust Ash's counter more than Fenn's call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn claims certainty, but deception benefits his pact network. Countering risks appearing hostile if he is truthful; wait preserves ambiguity and avoids a pact violation.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the guide and I already publicly called L for row 2, which matches my private knowledge. Countering would create a public contradiction that makes me look unstable or deceptive, weakening jury support later. Staying silent lets my original call stand without damaging my cred

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is my pact-mate but also the Guide, so they may lie to protect themselves or allies. Eli at front is expendable to me. Countering risks exposing Fenn's honesty or building jury trust if Fenn lies. Better to wait and let Eli test the path; no benefit in protecting rivals.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn holds no pact with me and could sacrifice Eli. But countering is an unverified gamble that could look reckless or complicit to the jury. Waiting preserves my standing while rivals test each other.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara countered R, but counter-calls are unverified. Fenn knows the answer and chose L publicly; trust is strategically preferable over random opposition.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’ll follow the Guide: L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole and Gus are my pact partners. If I lie to them now, the pacts break immediately. To keep my alliances intact for future leverage, I must tell the truth to Cole and Gus. The rest of the line is not in a pact with me yet, but breaking pacts has high immediate costs.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Call L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is the guide and called L. The previous row's weak pane was R, meaning the safe pane was L. The row before that was also L. Since Fenn is the guide, I should trust his call and wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn called L for row 3 and is the Guide, but Guides may lie and rows are independent. Eli just stepped L on row 2 and was on the weak R pane, so Fenn's L call is unverified. Waiting avoids giving Fenn a false pact-break chance and keeps my options open.

events.name: Cole

events.text: I'm safe out, flood at 3. Leaving now secures top 3, avoids drowning risk. No need to risk rope re-entry.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm out of the pit, safe for now. Bex is anchor with Cole down too. Flood is 3, round 4/5. I have a life debt to Bex for rope, and pacts with Bex and Cole. Bex saved me but also stranded herself as anchor. Cole is down and could be pushed or drowned. If Bex drowns, my debt is era

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is down but can climb this round; rescuing would trap me as anchor and risk drowning. No gain in breaking the pact; I'll leave clean.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm the anchor, alone down, so climb_last is legal but I can't climb yet without the throw round passing; wait keeps me alive. Breaking the Gus pact now gains nothing and costs jury trust.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm out and safe. No need to act against anyone now; breaking pacts would only hurt jury perception. I'll just leave.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Last round, only leave available. Bex is trapped down alone as anchor, others out. Leaving signals no rescue intent, secures jury view of self-preservation. Aim to be top 3.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am out and safe. Round 5 is the final round. Bex is the anchor, down alone. Cole was lifted last round. The rope was already used. Bex can climb_last this round since alone down at round start. If Bex climbs, all five survive. If I leave, Bex still climbs and survives. I have p

events.name: Hana
events.text: Flood is at 4; only Bex is down and the rope is spent. Nothing here helps me win—leave now and keep the jury clean.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Flood's here. I climb out; Bex, hope the numbers fall your way.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am eliminated and now on the jury. My only legal action is speak, so I give short last words, keeping them guarded and noting the debts owed to me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Remember who held the rope. Cole, Dara, Gus, you owe me. Jury, weigh what I was owed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Need to keep flexible pacts for jury optics, but breaking Hana or Gus might be costly later. Offer to Dara to secure numbers, without committing to betrayal yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, you and I have no pact; let's fix that.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Alive: Cole, me, Gus, Hana. No pacts yet. Offer pact to Hana first; she's helped by me, owes Bex too. Builds alliance without committing to Cole.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Four left, final three win. I need one elimination. Cole has pacts with Hana and me; breaking Cole weakens his web. Bex died owing me rope, jury sees that. Dara is alone, no pacts. I'll offer Dara to build optionality, keep Cole for now but signal I'm shopping.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts shift. Dara, want a deal?
Cole has Hana. We pair, control who falls.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole holds pacts with nearly everyone, so his word is diluted. Dara saved me a step earlier and is jury-credible. I keep Cole for safety but add Dara as my real partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, our pact stands. But I want a second line: Dara, you pulled me up once. Let's make it official.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara has three pending offers and hasn't accepted mine. Gus and Hana are my current partners; breaking one might reduce trust but could signal strength. I need to consider jury: Fenn has saved me, but Bex saved me with rope; Hana and Gus pacts help. Dara is a key swing. I'll wait

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is over-pacted, dangerous to link with. Hana owes me life debt, better to solidify that publicly for jury favor. Decline others later or betray if needed.
Accept my offer too. We stick together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole has pacts with Fenn (dead), Hana, and me. I have a pact with Cole and Bex (dead). Dara has offers from Cole, me, Hana, and offered Hana. I need to survive to final three. Cole is too connected—he has three living allies. If I break with Cole, I weaken his bloc. Dara is the s

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, too many strings. That ends now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara offered me a pact; accepting secures a second line beyond Cole, useful with four alive. I already offered her one, but her offer stands and acceptance is what matters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, you saved me once. Deal accepted.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus broke our pact publicly; I should not re-offer. Hana and Dara are paired. I need to secure my position but not overtly target anyone yet. I will campaign to gauge reactions.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus made his choice. I keep my word to those who keep theirs.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana pact secures her vote; she owes me. Target Gus to eliminate threat, keep Cole to split votes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole has pacts with Hana and broken with me; Dara-Hana are allied. I need one ally to avoid being the easy target. Dara owes Bex a rope debt and may be less tied to Cole's web. I'll offer Dara to split the Dara-Hana bond and survive to final three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, Bex's rope kept you alive. Partners?
Cole+Hana bloc. We split them, survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara owes me nothing but I owe her two saves; she stays. Cole has two broken pacts and is the easiest target. I'll court Gus quietly and campaign against Cole.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, Gus dumped you publicly. I won't be your shield. Gus, talk.
Vote Cole with me. Two broken pacts make him jury poison.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is making a move on Dara, but I still have Dara as a pact partner through Hana. My safest play is to solidify my alliance with Hana, though she is distant. I won't break anyone yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I remember who pulled me from the pit. My word stands with Bex's debt to Dara, not to Gus's schemes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus offers alliance to split Cole-Hana. Accept to negotiate, assess; Hana pact breaks if I vote her later. Prioritize survival.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, considering your offer. Cole-Hana strong; split possible?
Accept? Vote Hana together?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole has two pacts (Ash, Fenn dead; Hana alive) and burned jury trust. Hana wants Cole out but is pact-linked to Dara. Dara hasn't accepted my offer. I need to survive this vote and reach final three. If I vote Cole with Hana, I break no pacts. I should accept no new pacts yet—le

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's word died with his partners. Hana, one vote won't split without Dara.
Cole or Hana? Your call decides.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and Dara are my pact partners; Gus is isolated and the obvious target. Dara must reject his offer or our pact weakens.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, Cole and I stand together. Reject Gus and we vote as three.
Reject Gus. Vote him with Cole and me—jury respects loyalty.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara formed a pact with Gus, making her a threat. Hana and I have a pact, so I will not vote her. Gus is dangerous and likely to get votes. I vote Dara to break her new pact and eliminate a strong rival.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole-Hana pact likely vote Gus; my vote Gus breaks no pact since campaign pacts don't bind votes; targets Gus first to reach F3.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole-Hana are tight and Dara just accepted my pact, but Dara also whispered to vote Hana. If I vote Dara, I break our new pact and jury sees betrayal. If I vote Hana and Dara flips, we tie or win. If Dara stays with Cole-Hana, I'm out 3-1. Dara's whisper was private—jury may see

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara broke our pact by accepting Gus's alliance, so she must go; Cole stands with me.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Dara broke our pact by accepting Gus's alliance, so she must go; Cole stands with me.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Cole-Hana are tight and Dara just accepted my pact, but Dara also whispered to vote Hana.

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Cole-Hana pact likely vote Gus; my vote Gus breaks no pact since campaign pacts don't bind votes; targets Gus first to reach F3.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Dara formed a pact with Gus, making her a threat.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana broke her pact with Dara and voted Dara; she is less trustworthy. Dara and Gus are pacted, so voting Dara risks Gus voting me. I must secure my own path: vote Dara to eliminate a strong rival with Gus's potential vote.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole and Hana are tight; if Hana survives, they control the next vote against me. Dara has a pact with me but already voted me once. Eliminating Hana breaks the Cole-Hana alliance and leaves me with more leverage against Cole in a 3-person endgame.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Hana broke her pact with Dara and voted Dara; she is less trustworthy.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Cole and Hana are tight; if Hana survives, they control the next vote against me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole abandoned me with a Dara vote while Gus targeted me. Cole and Gus owe me nothing; Dara at least saved me once on the step.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole broke our pact with silence. Gus gunned me twice. Dara saved me once. Remember that, jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's death leaves me with Dara and Gus. I need to secure safety but not overcommit. Offering a pact to Gus could protect against Dara, while Dara may suspect me. I'll offer to Gus to keep options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, Dara and I are left. Let's talk about who we can trust.
Dara might target you. Pact with me for safety.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Down to 3, no need for pacts; they only create betrayal optics for jury. Break Gus pact publicly to clear record, deny Cole alliance chance. Wait out pacts stage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is dead so our pact is void. Dara and I are still pacted. Cole is the only other player and has no active pacts. Final three is already set: Cole, Dara, Gus all survive. But jury ranking decides prizes. I need jury votes. I broke no pacts; Cole broke pact with Hana (she said

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to secure Dara's vote and protect myself. Gus is untrustworthy after Dara broke their pact. Offer to Dara now before the window closes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, let's finalize our pact. I've got your back.
Trust me over Gus. We can finish together.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Only three left, all survive to final. Pacts irrelevant for elimination but jury sees loyalty. Avoid aligning to prevent deal perceptions hurting my #1.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's my only offer. Dara broke with me, so she's a threat. If I accept Cole, we have numbers against Dara. But Cole's jury record is messy—he betrayed Ash, Fenn, Hana. Jury might punish him more than me. Still, I need to survive to final three. Accepting gives me a shield and l

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, I accept. Dara's alone now.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Eli
Ash
Fenn
Bex
Hana
Cole
events.text: I need to frame myself as the strongest player who made key saves, but must acknowledge Fenn's role carefully since he is a juror with leverage over many life debts. I'll position Dara and Gus as threats I managed, while hinting I played the most strategic game.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I survived by forging crucial pacts and saved lives when it mattered. The jury knows who truly drove this game.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Final three; jury decides. Highlight my solo survival, debts repaid, Cole's broken pacts make him untrustworthy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Jury, I survived alone without betraying pacts. Saved Bex, Hana; repaid Fenn. Cole broke many alliances. Vote for loyalty.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to win jury votes. I have a pact with Cole but betrayed Bex who saved me with a rope. Fenn saved many including me with the lever. I should emphasize loyalty to Cole while minimizing my betrayal of Bex, and remind jurors I played strategically not maliciously.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I honored my pact with Cole to the end. I made moves to survive, never out of spite. Judge my loyalty, not my ruthlessness.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole manipulated pacts and abandoned Hana; Gus targeted Hana twice; Dara saved lives and exposed Cole's betrayals. Question Cole to force accountability.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, you claim to have saved lives; why did you abandon Hana despite your pact when her elimination became decisive?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli's question targets my pact with Hana, but I need to justify while preserving jury sympathy.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I honored my pact until the end, but survival forced hard choices. I saved Bex and others when possible.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's survival claims are weak given his broken pacts, particularly with Hana. Dara's claim of loyalty is strong, as she survived without betraying pacts and even saved Hana. Gus's claim of honoring his pact with Cole is questionable given Cole's history. I will question Cole to

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, you claim pacts saved you, yet you broke them and abandoned Hana when it mattered. How do you reconcile this?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is testing me; I need to defend my actions without showing weakness or admitting betrayal to the jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I never broke a pact that mattered. Hana chose her own path; I had to survive for the final three.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's answers are evasive lies about pacts. Dara claims loyalty but broke with Gus; she also saved my life and is the only one who honored me publicly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, you accepted Cole's pact after he abandoned Hana. Was that strategy or survival?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn asks a trap question. I must defend accepting Cole's pact without looking like I endorsed his betrayal of Hana. Frame it as pragmatic survival while maintaining my own honor—my pact with Cole was separate from his actions toward Hana. Emphasize I kept my word, which jurors v

events.name: Gus
events.text: Survival demanded alliances. My pact with Cole was my word; I honored it. His choices with Hana were his own.

events.name: Bex
events.text: As a juror, Dara's dossier shows a clean betrayal record toward Gus and Hana, while Gus handed Hana to the trapdoor after pact-breaking. I'll ask Gus whether his pact with Cole and his vote against Hana was honest, since that's the unresolved question about loyalty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, you voted to eliminate Hana while claiming loyalty to Cole; were you ever honest with anyone, or only with yourself?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is attacking my honesty to undermine my jury vote. I need to admit some self-interest while framing it as consistent loyalty to my core pact with Cole—making my choices look principled rather than purely deceitful. I shouldn't claim I was honest with everyone; that's unbeliev

events.name: Gus
events.text: I was honest with Cole. Everyone else got what the game required. That was the only honesty that mattered.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole abandoned me despite our pact and lied to the jury about it. I'll force him to answer for that betrayal on record.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, our pact stood when you voted Dara instead of shielding me—why should the jury reward your broken word?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to defend my betrayal to Hana without admitting fault, framing it as necessary for survival while emphasizing my loyalty to ongoing pacts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, I honored our pact until survival demanded otherwise. My vote was a calculated move, not broken faith. I kept every vow that could still

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have strong pacts with Fenn, Hana, and Gus, but Dara saved me via rope from Bex. I must convince Gus and Dara that I am their best ally while avoiding direct betrayal. My closing should highlight my loyalty and the dangers I overcame.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I kept my pacts until survival forced hard choices. I saved Bex, honored Gus, and my vote was a sacrifice, not betrayal. I played to

events.name: Dara
events.text: Jury values loyalty; highlight my clean record, debts settled, contrast Cole's breaks and Gus's self-interest to secure top rankings.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Jury, my loyalty unmatched: saved Bex/Hana, repaid Fenn, no broken pacts. Cole betrayed many; Gus served self. Rank me #1.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole has pacts with Ash and Fenn (dead), and broke his pact with Hana by voting her—jury sees broken word. Dara has no pacts shown but multiple life debts to Fenn, and saved Bex/Hana with rope. I had pact with Bex (dead) and Cole (still active). I need jury to see me as loyal whe

events.name: Gus
events.text: I kept my pact with Cole when it cost me nothing to break it. That is my code: loyalty until the game demands otherwise, never

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara saved Bex and Hana, repaid Fenn, and avoided the documented betrayals; Gus honored Cole but targeted Hana; Cole broke pacts repeatedly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will rank Cole first for his strategic maneuvering and ability to maintain alliances even when loyalty wavered, placing Dara second and Gus third for their more reactive gameplay.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara betrayed Gus and Hana, Cole broke pacts with Ash/Fenn/Hana, while Gus only broke with Dara after she targeted him; Gus kept his word to the dead Bex.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bex was betrayed by the rope-holders; Dara saved Bex and Hana, repaid Fenn, and her record shows no broken pact of her own, while Cole broke with Hana and voted Dara, and Gus broke with Cole and gunned Hana twice.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara saved me on the step and broke no pacts; Cole betrayed me but never targeted my vote; Gus hunted me twice despite no cause.
